main_concerns.concern: Preparation was substituted for execution: the scan has not been started, prerequisite checks are asserted but not evidenced, and Cap granted itself final arbitration authority that conflicts with the constraint against blind veto.

All three new artifact files (old-redcap-360-scan-account.json, old-redcap-360-scan-lifecycle.json, old-redcap-360-scan-prism-request.json) are untracked (??) in git status — not a single one has been committed to develop. The HEAD commit (0c065ad) is about pre-revival infrastructure hardening, not the 360 scan. The main AI is declaring a scan as started based on ephemeral local files that describe the scan rather than executing it or even versioning the preparation. This is a plan dressed as a milestone.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Execute both prerequisite checks and include their passing output in evidence; replace Cap's unilateral final arbitration with an escalation rule to Norven when bounded Prism discussion fails to reach consensus; include either the full scan account contents or a cryptographic manifest proving the seven shards exactly cover all known pre-revival issues.

1) Commit the three artifact files to develop with a clear commit message. 2) Actually run `runtime/bin/redcap prism-shard check` and `runtime/bin/redcap phase2-blueprint check` and attach their real stdout/stderr output — not just list the command strings as evidence. 3) Verify that assets/contracts/redcap-1.1-phase2-blueprint.json exists on disk (it doesn't appear in git status at all) and confirm the claimed four pathology shards are present in prior_decisions. 4) Only then declare readiness, not start — readiness is a state of prepared artifacts, start requires execution.
